author: Wilfred Owen
title: Poems
edition: Poems by Wilfred Owen, with an introduction by Siegfried Sassoon (London: Chatto & Windus, 1920; printed by Morrison and Gibb, Edinburgh), as transcribed by Project Gutenberg (eBook 1034). The library holds Sassoon’s introduction, Owen’s unfinished preface with its note, and the twenty-four poems in printed order, including the other version and alternative line printed after “Strange Meeting”; poem titles keep the transcription’s capitalisation. Project Gutenberg printed italics as capitals: the one such word, “aren’t” in “The Dead-Beat”, is given as _aren’t_, which the 1920 OCR shows as italic; “GAS!” in “Dulce et Decorum est” is in capitals in the print and stands. “Anthem for Doomed Youth”, “The Send-off” and “Disabled” were collated on 2026-11-18 against the OCR of Internet Archive poemsowenwil00owenrich, a copy of the 1920 Chatto & Windus edition, and against its page images (pp. 11–12 and 32–33): the transcription agrees with the print in every word and point; the OCR’s full stops for commas in “Disabled” are its own misreadings.

rights.basis: Owen’s Poems, with Sassoon’s introduction, was first published in London in 1920 (a US edition followed in 1921); both were published before 1931, and their US copyright terms have expired. Owen died in 1918. Project Gutenberg identifies this transcription as public domain in the USA.

acquisition.method: Project Gutenberg 1034 plain text (UTF-8) from the PG mirror aleph.pglaf.org (this old eBook has no cache/epub plain-text file there). Took the text from Sassoon’s “Introduction” to the end of “The End”; the PG header and footer, the title lines, the transcriber’s note on the text, the contents list, the “POEMS” divider, PG’s “[End of original text.]” and its appendix on later editions were dropped. Unindented one-line titles became level-2 headings (with “S. I. W.”), the roman section numbers of “Insensibility” and “Exposure” level-3 headings; indented line groups became stanzas, one line per verse line, indentation removed and runs of spaces closed up; prose paragraphs were joined with single spaces; the signature, dated lines, and the labels “Another Version” and “Alternative line--”, which PG marks as italic with *asterisks* (here _underscores_), are paragraphs. Double hyphens stand for dashes as transcribed.
